original_intent: Adaptive throughput, mobile participation, low resource cost and explicit security; outperform comparable networks
current_implementation: Local signed-proposal DAG; no global finality; classical Ed25519
comparison_requirements: same hardware allocations and total machine budget
same network topology, bandwidth, delay, loss and partitions
same user transaction payload, signatures, witnesses and conflict ratio
same commit predicate and receipt validation
same data availability, pruning, recovery and retention obligations
same membership, adversary, corruption and fault assumptions
same offered load, interval, warmup and inclusion definition

finality_latency_p50_p95_p99_ms.clock: client submission through independently verified final receipt

units: peak RSS/private bytes of process tree
CPU seconds per successful finalized user transaction
ingress/egress bytes per role and useful transaction

metrics: safe status/cancel feedback on slow signing
p95 render frame time separate from block cadence

security.gate: specified model, invariants and independent protocol review; no universal 10x-security scalar

test_stages.limits: finite signed DAG; no remote adversary/global finality

test_stages.stage: independent Linux Windows physical Termux devices

test_stages.report: all trials, median, distributions, uncertainty and failures

adaptive_capacity.meaning: No arbitrary universal throughput target; each node retains authenticated resource and parser limits
adaptive_capacity.slow_signing: status or cancel; no automatic second economic transaction

claim_policy.tenfold: Only a named metric with comparable recorded runs meeting requirements, not a blanket protocol guarantee
claim_policy.unknown: UNKNOWN or INCOMPARABLE, never zero cost or PASS
claim_policy.quantum: No PQ claim from Merkle trees or metadata alone
